 Tenerife to Experience a Sunny Saturday with Rising Temperatures and Possible Dust Haze
 November 20, 2026 
 in 
 El Dia 
 Reading Time: 2 mins read
 0 
 3 
 SHARES 
 Share on Facebook Share on Twitter 
 Tenerife is set for a sunny Saturday, November 21, with temperatures rising slightly. However, the State Meteorological Agency (Aemet) warns of possible light calima, or dust haze, in the latter part of the day, which may also affect other western islands.

 Throughout the day, expect mostly clear skies with some high clouds. The eastern coast may see low clouds in the early hours and later in the day.
 One significant feature of the forecast is the potential for light calima in the afternoon, although Aemet has not confirmed this.
 Temperatures are expected to remain stable, with minimal changes in the coastal areas, where there could be a slight decline. In contrast, the midlands and higher areas may experience a moderate rise. In Santa Cruz de Tenerife, temperatures will range from 19 to 24 degrees Celsius.
 Winds will be light to moderate, generally coming from an east to northeast direction, while central summits may experience westerly winds.
 The rest of the Canary Islands will also see stable weather, with mostly clear skies punctuated by high clouds. Light calima is possible in La Gomera and El Hierro during the afternoon as well.
 In Gran Canaria, expect mostly clear skies with some high clouds. The northern and eastern coasts may have low clouds early and late in the day. Minimum temperatures will change little, while maximums may drop slightly along the coasts but rise in midlands and higher regions. In Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, temperatures are forecasted to be between 21 and 25 degrees Celsius.
 Lanzarote and Fuerteventura will experience generally clear conditions with high clouds, and some low clouds along the northern and eastern coasts at times. Maximum temperatures may rise slightly in Fuerteventura’s interior and Lanzarote’s inland areas, while minimums will likely stay the same or decrease slightly. Arrecife will experience temperatures ranging from 19 to 24 degrees, and Puerto del Rosario will see between 21 and 24 degrees.
 La Palma is expected to have mostly clear skies with high clouds and low clouds on the northern and eastern coasts in the morning and late hours. Temperatures will change little, with possible slight decreases in minimums, reaching between 18 and 22 degrees in Santa Cruz de La Palma.
 La Gomera will see a similar forecast, with mostly clear skies, some high clouds, and low clouds along the coasts, especially in the east. Aemet indicates a possibility of light calima in the afternoon. Maximum temperatures will rise slightly in midlands and higher areas, ranging from 18 to 24 degrees in San Sebastián de La Gomera.
 Lastly, El Hierro is set for a day with mostly clear skies and intervals of high clouds. Low clouds may appear in coastal areas, particularly in the north and east, alongside potential light calima in the afternoon. In Valverde, temperatures will range from 15 to 22 degrees.
